correction.text: The 1260 shape unchanged, the county of Orange around the town, drawn from the elevation to a principality in 1163

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1163-1259: the 1260 shape drawn from the elevation of the county of Orange to a principality. infobox 'Principality status granted: 1163'; Frederick I raised the county to a principality, held as a fief of the Holy Roman Empire. Area: infobox 108 sq mi (280 km2), the article body says 180 km2; Cliopatria 234 km2 for 1260-1271 (ratio 0.84 to the infobox), inside the factor of two.

234 km2 against 280 km2 (infobox) and 180 km2 (body): ratio 0.84 and 1.3, inside the factor of two. In 1256 Lord Guillaume des Baux paid a tribute to the seneschal of Provence at Villebois-les-Pins, a tribute from a fief of the Empire, not a loss of land.

140.5 km2: ratio 0.50 to the infobox's 280 km2 (the edge of the factor of two) and 0.78 to the body's 180 km2. The smaller shape from 1272 is not explained by any page opened (the pages date no change of land between 1163 and 1544); kept as the Cliopatria shape.
140.5 km2, the same land. The Baux (1173) gave way to the Chalons in 1393 ('passed to the French noble houses of Baux, in 1173, and of Chalons, in 1393'); the pages date no change of land in 1459.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, to be drawn 1564-1713: the principality of Orange under the House of Orange-Nassau, until the Treaty of Utrecht

keyframe_review.note: 140.5 km2. Cliopatria ends the row in 1571, but the principality continued: William the Silent inherited it in 1544, Louis XIV's forces captured it in 1672 and again in August 1682, and it was ceded to France in 1713 (Treaty of Utrecht). The shape is unchanged and holds to 1713.

region.text: the county raised to a principality, with the town of Orange as capital

ledger.note: 1163: Frederick I raises the county of Orange to a principality, held as a fief of the Holy Roman Empire. infobox 'Principality status granted: 1163'; the article's history says Frederick I raised the county to a principality that year.

1393: the principality passes from the Baux to the Chalons. 'The title and land passed to the French noble houses of Baux, in 1173, and of Chalons, in 1393' (the infobox gives the first ruler, Bertrand I of Baux, as 1171-1185). The House of Baux page lists 'Mary of Baux-Orange(1393–1417), daughter, married John III of Chalon-Arlay' and says 'In 1417, the House of Ivrea or House of Chalon-Arlay succeeded as princes of Orange': the Chalon succession is 1393 on the Prince of Orange page and 1417 on the House of Baux page, whose own list is inconsistent (Bertrand I 1167-1181 and 1171-1181); kept at 1393. Same state, same colour.

1544: William the Silent inherits Orange. William the Silent, aged 11, inherited the principality from his cousin René of Châlon, who died that year (Principality page) (the Prince of Orange page: 'in 1544 to the Dillenburg branch of the House of Nassau'). Same state, same colour.

region.text: the whole principality, captured and repeatedly reoccupied by French forces

ledger.note: 1672: Louis XIV's forces take Orange. Louis XIV's forces under the Comte de Grignan captured the principality and the citadel was later besieged and destroyed; they captured it again in August 1682, when William did not give up his claim (Principality page). The other pages give 1673 (annexed by Louis XIV) and occupations in 1673, 1679, 1690, 1697 and 1702-1713. [Reviewer eu-10-g: contest region set to the 1564 shape (140.5 km2), the one drawn 1564-1713, instead of the 1260 shape (234 km2) that reaches outside it.]

1713: the Treaty of Utrecht ends the contest. The Treaty of Utrecht ceded the principality to France (Principality page); Louis XIV had enfeoffed the Prince of Conti after William III died childless in 1702, and bestowed the usufruct on Louis Armand of Bourbon, Prince de Conti, in 1714 (Prince of Orange page).

1713: Orange is ceded to France. 'Ceded to France: 1713, under the Treaty of Utrecht'; Frederick I (Prince of Orange page: Frederick William I) of Prussia ceded the territory but kept the princely title. After the Revolution it joined the Drôme département in 1790 (later Vaucluse).

wars.name: French conquest and occupations of Orange
wars.outcome: Captured by Louis XIV's forces in 1672 and again in August 1682; occupied by France in 1673, 1679, 1690, 1697 and 1702-1713, and ceded to France in 1713 under the Treaty of Utrecht, the Prussian king keeping the title.
wars.note: The pages give different dates: 1672 and 1682 (Principality page), annexation in 1673 (Prince of Orange page), occupations in 1673, 1679, 1690, 1697 and 1702-1713 (Orange, Vaucluse page); the Principality page names Frederick I and the Prince of Orange page Frederick William I as the ceding Prussian king. The war itself is not named on any page opened.

certainty.note: A 140-280 km2 enclave: the boundaries are communal and no page gives a boundary line. The infobox and body disagree on the area (280 and 180 km2).

notes: Cliopatria ends the row in 1571 (shapes 1260-1571, a single 140-234 km2 cell near Orange) but the principality lasted to 1713; the last keyframe is extended to 1713 and the contest 1672-1713 recorded. Not settled: why the shape shrinks from 234 to 140.5 km2 in 1272; why Cliopatria stops in 1571 (the pages give no 1571 event; 'Wars of Religion' damage and the Protestant side are undated); the 1256 tribute to the seneschal of Provence (a tribute from a fief of the Empire, an Angevin claim of overlordship that belongs in capetian-house-of-anjou, not recorded there for lack of a matching end date); the Baux dates (1173 on the Prince of Orange page, first ruler Bertrand I 1171-1185 on the infobox, 1167-1181 or 1171-1181 on the House of Baux page) and the Chalon succession (1393 or 1417: the House of Baux page lists Mary of Baux-Orange 1393-1417 and the Chalon-Arlay succession in 1417); the Prussian king who ceded Orange (Frederick I or Frederick William I); the Dauphiné administration of Orange (Orange, Vaucluse page) against the Cliopatria relation 'member of the Holy Roman Empire' 1260-1458. No ruler strip: the pages give a first and a last ruler (Bertrand I of Baux 1171-1185; William III 1650-1702) but no list. Orange is an enclave in the Comtat Venaissin (comtat-venaissin, 1272-1790): the two rows touch.
